header.name: Applied Optimization methods for machine learning (AOMML)
header.description: In this course, we will discuss the foundations required for solving optimization problems in the context of machine learning through various case-studies/running-examples. This course will cover basics of linear algebra required for learning optimization theory. Further, this course provides a platform to set up an optimization problem, which could be linear and nonlinear; unconstrained and constrained; convex and non-convex; continuous and discrete; deterministic and stochastic. We also cover the machine learning based context of different topics.
prerequisites_desirable: Good to have a background in Convex Optimization and Linear Optimization.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to formulate and solve optimization problems for training machine learning models.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to implement optimization algorithms like stochastic gradient descent, Newton's method, etc.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to derive the convergence properties (Order and rate for non-asymptotic, otherwise asymptotic convergence) of optimization algorithms based on their analytical properties (convexity, smoothness, optimality conditions).

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to develop insights into applying suitable optimization algorithms for a given machine-learning task.

lecture_topics: Basic Linear Algebra (Vectors, Vector spaces and subspaces, Rank, Orthogonality of vectors)
Basic multi-variable calculus (Gradient, Jacobian, Hessian, Semidefinite matrices)
Motivation: Training machine/deep learning models as an Optimization problem
First-order methods: Proximal Gradient Descent, Stochastic Gradient Descent
Variants of Gradient Descent: Projected, Accelerated
Variants of Stochastic Gradient Descent: Minibatch, Momentum, Adaptive Momentum, YOGI
Second Order Methods: Newton's Method, Quasi-Newton's Method
Advanced Techniques: Mirror Descent, Dual Decomposition
Advanced Techniques: Alternative direction method of multipliers, Frank Wolfe method

Gilbert Strang, Linear Algebra and its Applications 4 Edition
Nocedal and Wright’s Numerical Optimization, Second Edition: https://users.iems.northwestern.edu/~nocedal/book/num-opt.html
Sebastian Bubeck: Convex Optimization: Algorithms and Complexity
